title: First-party web UI providers for embedded, browser, and terminal targets
question: Which first-party web UI provider layers can expose one host-agnostic Last Light application without promoting a W API, syntax, or specification?
candidateLayers: host-agnostic web UI application and assets
crosspoints: signed registry asset digests and CSP
terminal UI semantics and live state
benchmarkReason: This registration records planned performance axes only. It contains no timing, result, or performance claim.

officialRefs.claim: Tauri combines a Rust host, HTML in an OS WebView, and message passing.
Capabilities grant or deny permissions for selected windows or WebViews.
Wry is a Rust cross-platform WebView library that needs an event loop and window handle.
webview is a C/C++ HTML5 abstraction using WebKit on Linux and macOS and WebView2 on Windows.
WebViewJS provides a cross-platform WebView library for Node, Deno, and Bun.
Wails targets desktop applications built with Go and web technologies.
Neutralino uses a layered core with HTTP web resources and WebSocket native API messages.
Electron separates main and renderer processes and can isolate utility work.
Electron security depends on Chromium, Node.js, Electron, dependencies, and application code.
Production WebView2 apps use the WebView2 Runtime rather than the installed Edge Stable channel.
Hosted web content can reach native resources unless a WebView2 app isolates it correctly.
WKWebView is Apple's WebKit view for displaying web content inside an app.
WebKitGTK WebView manages content drawing, events, URI or data loading, and settings.
Android WebView embeds web content and supports URL navigation through the Android APIs.
WebUI can use an installed browser or optional WebView and exposes a WebSocket bridge.
CEF embeds Chromium-based browsers in other applications.
Qt WebEngine uses Chromium and profiles can isolate pages, settings, scripts, and cookies.
Servo intends to be embeddable, while its embedding documentation remains sparse and in progress.
Carbonyl is a Chromium-based browser that runs in a terminal.
Browsh renders interactive modern web pages to TTYs using headless Firefox.
Browsh's CLI starts a compatible headless browser and connects through remote debugging.
Lynx is a text web browser and supplies a conservative terminal baseline.
WAI-ARIA defines accessibility semantics and an accessibility tree model for user agents and assistive technology.

stopCondition: Stop on stale references, missing provider receipts, failed real-provider smoke, failed security adversarial cases, unsupported terminal promises, or any request to promote an API, syntax, or specification before Sol and human review.
